newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down, gilts up in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down, gilts up in light trade.

text.p: Indian call money eased to end Monday at 8.0-8.25 percent from opening quotes of 8.5-9.5 percent on borrower resistance to higher rates, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was done between 8.25 and 8.5 percent, with stray deals at 8.0 percent.
"Rates were a bit high to start with as lenders were quoting on the higher side," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But they soon came down as borrowers were unwilling to pay higher rates."
He said market sentiment had improved and rates were seen lower in coming days.

"The general feeling among market players is that at current liquidity levels, call money should be in the 6.0-8.0 percent range," he said. "Further there is an inflow of about 10 billion rupees by way of interest payments on government securities during the next two weeks."
Call money was below 1.0 percent for most of April before shooting up in the past two weeks, touching 10.5 percent last Monday.
Dealers said prices of government securities rose marginally in moderate trade.
"There was some buying interest today as call money eased and market expectations are that it will ease further," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But trades were poor."
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock rose to 101.95 rupees from 101.80 and the 13.12 percent 1999 to 103.05 from 102.55, dealers said.
The 12.69 percent 2002, issued at par on Friday, was traded at 100.25, they said.
